transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: I hear you—there’s a lot of junk out there. When a call comes in and nobody picks up, what happens today: do they hit voicemail, go to a cell, or just… disappear?
User: They mostly disappear. Voicemail's a black hole. But how do I know you're not just a robot recording this?
Agent: Yeah, I am—I’m Linda, an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux, and I handle the intro and getting you set up with a live walkthrough. What kind of business is this for?
User: Ortiz Roofing, Dallas. But who's seeing my data? I don't want my customers getting calls from some robot.
Agent: Got it—Ortiz Roofing in Dallas, and yeah, protecting customer info matters. When a new lead calls you, do you want us to only answer inbound calls (so nobody’s getting “robot” outbound calls), or are there any follow-ups you’d actually want placed?
User: Only inbound. No robots calling my customers. How do I know you're not recording this right now?
Agent: Totally fair—yes, this call may be recorded by the phone carrier or our call system for quality, but we’re not using it to spam your customers, and we can keep the setup to inbound-only so nobody gets outbound “robot calls.”  

Is your main concern here privacy/recording specifically, or more that customers might feel weird talking to an automated receptionist?
User: My main concern is privacy and how my data is used. Who's accessing it?
Agent: Makes sense. When you say “my data,” are you most concerned about the call audio itself, or the customer details we collect (name, phone, address, job info)?
User: Both, honestly. But especially customer details. I don't want them mishandled or used without my consent.
Agent: Got it—especially the customer details and consent. Do you want it set up so only you and your team can access the caller info, and we don’t use it for anything outside handling your inbound calls?
User: Sounds better, but how do I know this isn't just another scam? What's the catch here?
Agent: I hear you—no catch: you stay in control of who can access customer details, and we keep it inbound-only so we’re not blasting your list. What would you need to see or hear to feel confident this is legit—proof of how data is handled, or proof it actually captures jobs you’re currently missing?
User: Show me how much money I'm missing out on and prove my data stays secure.
Agent: Absolutely—let’s put a real number on it first. Ballpark, how many calls per week hit voicemail or go unanswered—10, 20, 30?
User: About 30 calls a week. But explain how my data is safe and no robots call my clients.
Agent: Got it—30 a week. Quick follow-up so I can quantify it: of those missed calls, what percent do you think would’ve turned into a booked job if you’d answered—half (50%)?
User: More like 40%. But I'm still wary about how this whole thing protects my data and privacy.
Agent: Makes sense—you shouldn’t do this unless you’re confident on privacy. Last number for the math: what’s your average roofing ticket—roughly $6,000, $10,000, or $15,000?
User: Around $1,800. But I'm not convinced yet. How do I know this isn't some trick to get my info?
Agent: Totally hear you. Based on 30 missed calls a week, 40% close rate, and $1,800 average ticket, you’re leaking about **$93,500/month**—and we can keep it **inbound-only** so nobody’s getting outbound “robot calls,” with access limited to your team.  

It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how data access works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, I'll bite. Let's do the walkthrough. Tomorrow works. Call me at +14695550001.
Agent: Got it—tomorrow works, and I’ll use **(469) 555-0001**. What time tomorrow is best for you, and are you on Central time in Dallas?
User: Yes, Central time. Let’s do 10 AM. But remember, no robots or funny business with my data.
Agent: Got it—10 AM Central, and inbound-only with strict access to your customer data. What’s your first name?
User: Sam, but let's keep everything above board. Just the live call, no gimmicks.
Agent: Got it, Sam—straight, above board. What’s the name of your company?
User: Ortiz Roofing, Dallas. But keep it simple—just the live call, no data tricks or AI gimmicks.
Agent: Got it, Sam—keeping it simple. For tomorrow (Wednesday), I can do **11:45 AM** or **12:30 PM** Central time—what works?
User: Let's go with 11:45 AM Central. But remember, no funny business with my data or customer privacy.
Agent: Got it—so that’s **tomorrow (Wed 8/26) at 11:45 AM Central**, correct?
User: Yes, that works. Just make sure my data is protected and no AI shenanigans.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now. I can try **tomorrow at 12:30 PM Central** instead—does that work?
User: Alright, but let's keep it straightforward. No surprises or hidden terms, just the live call.
Agent: One moment while I lock that in.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now. I can try **tomorrow at 12:30 PM Central** instead—does that work?
User: Fine, but remember—no AI trickery or data misuse. Just the live call, straightforward and secure.
Agent: Got it, Sam—straightforward and secure is the goal. My calendar isn’t letting me confirm it right this second, so let’s try a different slot: tomorrow at 12:30 PM Central. If that works, I’ll lock it in while you’re here—thanks for your patience, and talk soon.
